name: Guarding Against Steering
title: Guarding Against Steering
answer: Guarding against steering means watching whether college and career guidance tools push students toward some paths and away from others based on old patterns in their data. It matters because a tool can quietly suggest less ambitious options to students from certain backgrounds, and a counselor's encouragement can change a student's path in ways no tool can.

sections.body: Guidance tools that recommend colleges or careers can steer students in ways that are hard to notice. When a tool learns from past data, it may repeat old patterns, offering less ambitious options to students from some backgrounds. This is a problem because the student may treat the suggestion as a limit rather than a starting point. Counselors therefore need to guard against steering rather than assume the tool is neutral. The idea asks schools to treat recommendations as something to question, not something to accept.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In practice, counselors check recommendations for patterns rather than reviewing them one at a time. They ask whether students from different groups receive similar suggestions when their interests and records are similar. They look for signs that girls are steered away from engineering or that students from low income families are steered away from selective colleges. These questions are meant to get regular attention, not a single review. Counselors also tell students that recommendations are starting points, not verdicts, and encourage them to consider options they had not imagined. The text does not give grade band examples for this idea.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book labels this idea with research it described in Chapter 15, which showed that balanced data does not guarantee fair results (Li et al., 2026). The finding is stated as a caution: even when the data behind a tool is balanced, the results it produces may still be unfair. The text does not offer further studies, figures, or numbers for this idea beyond that citation.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The limits here are that a tool's suggestions can carry old patterns forward, and that no tool can supply the encouragement a trusted adult gives a student. The decisions stay with people. Counselors must watch for steering, check recommendations for patterns across groups, and keep asking the questions the text sets out. Students should always know that recommendations are starting points rather than verdicts, and a counselor can push a student to look beyond what the tool suggests. High expectations from a trusted adult remain something the tool cannot provide.
